title: Perf-canary gate: enforce selector v2 p95 regression budgets in CI
creator: Marcus Reed
related_links: Confluence: Kernel selector v2 benchmark plan (sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/kernel-selector-v2-benchmark-plan.json)
description:
Goal
- Add a CI gate that blocks merges / release promotion when kernel selector v2 causes p95 latency or throughput regressions beyond defined budgets.
- Gate should be stable (low flake rate), fast enough to run on PRs that touch selector/registry/scheduler paths, and strict enough to catch the A10 long-context regression class we saw during early canary.

Context
- Selector v2 changes are high leverage and high risk: small registry changes can shift kernel choice for common workloads and produce tail latency regressions.
- We need an automated guardrail in addition to benchmark reports and manual dashboards.

What this ticket delivers
1) Perf-canary job: selector_v2_gate
- A dedicated job in perf-canary that runs a pinned benchmark matrix and compares against a blessed baseline.
- Produces a single pass/fail verdict plus a markdown/JSON artifact with detailed deltas.

2) Budgets / thresholds (first cut)
- Metrics evaluated per scenario (model family x seq bucket x GPU SKU), plus an aggregate “overall” view.
- Default budgets (initial proposal; adjust based on observed noise once we have 10+ stable runs):
  - p95 latency: regression must be <= +7% (fail if > +7%)
  - tokens/sec (throughput): regression must be <= -5% (fail if < -5%)
  - Additionally: hard fail if p95 latency regression is > +12% for any long-context bucket (these are the incidents that hurt Dedicated customers the most).
- Scenarios included in the gate (v0):
  - GPU SKUs: L4, A10, A100, H100
  - Model families: Llama-family, Mistral-family, Qwen-family (as entries exist in the registry)
  - Seq buckets: short prefill, long prefill, steady-state decode

3) Flake/noise controls
- Each scenario runs N=3 trials; compare median of trials to reduce variance.
- Minimum sample size requirements: fail closed if a scenario produces too few requests/tokens to make p95 meaningful.
- Warmup handling: discard first W requests per worker to reduce cold-start artifacts.
- Explicitly pin: runtime build, driver/cuda, and benchmark harness version.

4) Baseline + update process
- Baseline is a blessed artifact produced from main on a known-good commit (baseline_commit).
- Baseline updates are only allowed via a dedicated “Update baseline” workflow and require:
  - a PR description explaining why the new performance is acceptable
  - sign-off from Runtime Perf (Marcus Reed) + SRE observer (Aisha Bello or Allison Grant delegate)
- Baseline artifacts are stored with a retention policy and include: commit SHA, GPU info, harness version, and summary stats.

5) CI wiring / when it runs
- Runs on:
  - PRs labeled: kernel-selector, runtime-perf, kernel-registry, scheduler-perf
  - Any changes under selector v2 codepaths / registry schema / scheduler signals
  - Release train promotion for runtime-1.19 candidates
- Provides a clear failure message with:
  - top 10 worst regressions
  - pointers to the per-scenario report artifact
  - guidance for local repro via benchmark-lab

Non-goals
- Not a full replacement for periodic wide benchmark sweeps (this gate is a focused “smoke + budget” check).
- Not doing cost/token attribution in the gate v0 (we’ll add later once variance is understood).

Open questions / follow-ups
- Do we gate on absolute latency targets (SLO-style) or only relative regressions? For v0: relative vs baseline.
- Whether to add a correctness signal (NaN/overflow) here vs separate conformance tests (currently handled in ENG-3928; we can add a hard fail if harness detects NaNs).

Acceptance criteria
- Gate runs in CI and produces deterministic pass/fail with <2% flake rate across a week of PR traffic.
- Gate catches known regression classes:
  - A10 long-context p95 regressions
  - mis-bucketed seq regime leading to wrong decode kernel
- Documentation exists for:
  - interpreting results
  - temporarily bypassing (only via explicit override label + required approvers)
  - updating the baseline with sign-off

Notes for release engineering
- This gate should be required for runtime-1.19 branch cut and for any post-cut selector/registry changes.
- In emergency rollback scenarios, the gate should not block disabling selector v2 (kill switch changes should be exempt / fast-path).
comments: 2026-01-23 (Marcus Reed): Creating this after the canary regression thread. We need a hard CI stop for selector/registry changes. Sahana can you own perf-canary integration and CI wiring?

2026-01-27 (Sahana Iyer): Ack. I’ll build it in perf-canary as a dedicated workflow. Need from runtime: the exact scenario list we consider “must not regress” + expected run-to-run variance so we don’t create a flaky gate.

2026-02-02 (Sana Farid): Please include an explicit “long-context on A10” hard threshold. That was the customer-visible p95 issue; relative-only thresholds risk being too lenient if baseline is already bad for a SKU.
2026-02-06 (Rina Kobayashi): benchmark-lab matrix PR is up; can reuse the same scenario YAML for the gate. For H100 we might need to cap concurrency to avoid queueing artifacts.
2026-02-11 (Aisha Bello): From SRE POV, require: (1) clear rollback path, (2) baseline update requires approval, (3) gate should publish a linkable artifact in CI so oncall can debug quickly.

2026-02-18 (Sahana Iyer): Implemented gate in perf-canary PR #388 with initial budgets (+7% p95 latency / -5% tok/s). Artifact includes per-scenario tables + worst offenders. Waiting on Marcus to review budgets and on Rina to confirm the scenario YAML stability on A10 runners.

2026-02-24 (Marcus Reed): Reviewed PR #388. Main request: add minimum token threshold per scenario (we saw a false pass when long-context bucket only had ~30 samples). Also add a note on how to rerun the job against a different baseline for debugging. Otherwise looks good.
